title: State of Eritrea
capsule: Eritrea was an Italian colony from 1890 and came under British administration from 1941; the United Nations federated it with Ethiopia in 1952, and Emperor Haile Selassie unilaterally annexed it as an Ethiopian province in 1962. A thirty-year independence war followed, led principally by the Eritrean People's Liberation Front (EPLF); the EPLF achieved military victory in 1991 and independence was confirmed by referendum in April 1993, giving the country formal recognition from May 1993. Isaias Afwerki became president and the EPLF, renamed the People's Front for Democracy and Justice, consolidated a single-party state; a border war with Ethiopia (1998–2000) killed tens of thousands and left the boundary dispute legally settled but practically unimplemented until the 2018 peace agreement brokered under Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Eritrea's internationally recognised borders are defined by colonial-era treaties and the 2002 Eritrea-Ethiopia Boundary Commission ruling, though the Badme area was occupied by Ethiopia against the commission's award until 2018.
